events.title: The Great Fire of Rome Breaks Out
events.description: On the night of July 18, a fire erupted among the shops near the Circus Maximus in Rome. It spread quickly through the crowded, timber-built districts and burned for days. Large parts of the city were destroyed.
events.significance: The fire reshaped the capital and led to major changes in Roman building rules. Emperor Nero was widely blamed, and Christians were later persecuted as scapegoats.

events.title: Papal Infallibility Is Decreed
events.description: The First Vatican Council approved the dogma of papal infallibility on July 18. It holds that the pope cannot err when he formally defines doctrine on faith and morals.
events.significance: This was a landmark in modern Catholic doctrine and in the authority of the papacy. It also caused lasting debate and divisions within the Church.

events.title: Nelson Mandela Is Born
events.description: Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela was born on July 18 in the village of Mvezo in South Africa's Eastern Cape. He grew up to lead the struggle against apartheid.
events.significance: Mandela spent 27 years in prison and became South Africa's first democratically elected president. His birthday is now marked each year as Nelson Mandela International Day.

events.title: Mein Kampf Is Published
events.description: Adolf Hitler published the first volume of his manifesto, Mein Kampf, on July 18. It set out his racist ideology and his political ambitions.
events.significance: The book became a foundational text of Nazism. It is a stark reminder of how openly extremist ideas were published long before the catastrophe that followed.

events.title: Spanish Civil War Begins
events.description: A military coup against Spain's elected Republican government was planned for July 18, though it began a day earlier in Spanish Morocco. On July 18, General Francisco Franco broadcast a manifesto from the Canary Islands calling on the army to rise up.
events.significance: The failed coup turned into a three-year civil war. It ended with Franco's dictatorship, which ruled Spain for almost four decades.
